subject: Clarify EU-only compute, operator access, and SCCs addendum
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marc Donovan <marc@aureliatx.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify EU-only compute, operator access, and SCCs addendum

Hi Marc / Gillian,

Thanks for the quick read on our platform. Aurelia's security team mentioned a few open points after the initial questionnaire — specifically: (1) confirmation that inference compute for your tenant will remain in EU regions only, (2) limitations on operator (Redwood) access to customer data and KV caches, and (3) proposed contract language to reflect SCCs + additional safeguards for Schrems II concerns.

I've looped in Lauren (legal lead) and Ben (product/security lead) to help provide concrete answers and a draft addendum we can propose. Could you confirm whether you need: (a) operator access strictly limited to named Redwood personnel via IAM & emergency break-glass only, (b) KMS key custody in your Azure/AWS KMS (customer-managed), or (c) Redwood-managed KMS with HSM backed SLA? Any preference narrows the redline we'll send.

Attached: Aurelia_SCCS_Questionnaire.xlsx (your filled sheet).

If helpful, we can do a 30-min follow-up next week to walk the addendum.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marc Donovan <marc@aureliatx.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Gillian Kaye <gillian.kaye@aureliatx.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only compute, operator access, and SCCs addendum

Vanessa,

Appreciate the fast response. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec and Legal:

1) EU-only compute: we need a contractual guarantee that inference processing for Aurelia will be confined to EU data centers (Ireland/Frankfurt preferred) and that any failover to non-EU regions is explicitly forbidden except by pre-approved emergency process. Is Redwood able to add a binding in-region processing clause?

2) Operator access: can you confirm the exact roles and conditions under which Redwood engineers would have live access to customer model state, KV cache, or logs? We want operator access limited to named individuals with MFA, strict RBAC, and session recording. Also need auditability (who accessed what and when).

3) KMS: Our preference is customer-managed keys in our Azure tenant. If that's not viable for inference GPU nodes we need a clear custodian model (HSM-backed, dual-control, auditable key rotation, and export restrictions).

4) Backup & deletion: we require proof-of-deletion for backups and snapshots, including timestamps and deletion tokens for at-rest copies. Is a certified deletion certificate possible?

5) SCCs & Schrems II: our counsel wants explicit language about supplemental technical and organizational measures (STOMs) and an annex that names the subprocessor chain and limits onward transfers. Can Redwood produce a redline addendum we can feed to counsel?

I've attached our final questionnaire in case there are gaps. We're on a tight timeline for a board review on Oct 10 — ideally we'd have draft contract language and operational commitments before then.

Thanks — Marc
Security Director, Aurelia Therapeutics
Attachment: Aurelia_SCCS_Questionnaire.xlsx (updated)


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Clarify EU-only compute, operator access, and SCCs addendum

Team,

Draft responses and action items below for Vanessa to send to Aurelia. I'm attaching a first-pass redline (redwood-sccs-addendum-draft.docx) that addresses their five asks. Key points:

- EU-only compute: we can contractually commit to in-region processing limited to EU regions we operate (Ireland, Frankfurt). Addendum section 2.1 binds routing policy and obligates Redwood to notify Aurelia and obtain written approval before any cross-border failover except for narrowly defined emergency (e.g., total regional outage).

- Operator access: propose binding an "Operator Access Matrix" (Appendix A) that names roles (SRE oncall, security incident engineer) and requires: RBAC, MFA, Just-In-Time privileged escalation, session recording, and proofs of access including session logs for 24 months. Emergency break-glass requires dual-approval from Redwood Security and Aurelia-designated POC.

- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS for workload encryption on supported clouds. For cases where customer KMS isn't available for GPU nodes, propose a hybrid where customer provides envelope keys and Redwood uses HSM-backed keys under a dual-control policy — documented in Appendix B.

- Backup & deletion: we can provide deletion manifests (timestamped deletion events) for primary data stores and snapshots. For immutable backups retained for regulated reasons, we propose a retention carveout but will provide retention rationale and scheduled deletion dates. We cannot produce a cryptographic "certificate of deletion" for third-party cloud snapshots but can provide signed deletion manifests and audit logs.

- SCCs & STOMs: the addendum adds a STOMs annex (encryption, logging, geofencing, subprocessor list) and a subprocessors table with update cadence. We will include a 30-day notice window for subprocessor changes and a rights-to-audit clause constrained by mutual NDAs and scheduling.

Action items:
- Ben: finalize the Operator Access Matrix language and session log retention specifics (how logs are stored, retention policy, redaction rules).
- Jordan: confirm technical feasibility and config for customer-managed KMS on Aurelia's target infra; outline fallback exactly (envelope keys flow).
- Vanessa: propose the draft to Aurelia and schedule a 30-min call if they want a walkthrough.

Attachment: redwood-sccs-addendum-draft.docx

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marc Donovan <marc@aureliatx.com>, Gillian Kaye <gillian.kaye@aureliatx.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only compute, operator access, and SCCs addendum

Marc / Gillian,

Thank you — forwarding our proposed responses and an addendum draft for review (attached). Summary of the operational commitments in plain language:

• In-region processing: Redwood commits to running inference for Aurelia in EU regions only (Ireland/Frankfurt). Cross-border failover is prohibited unless both parties agree in writing or an explicit emergency process is invoked (emergency defined in Sec 7 of the addendum).

• Operator access: Access will be limited to named roles listed in Appendix A. All access requires MFA, RBAC, JIT approval, and session recording. We will provide session logs and an access report on request (30-day SLA for standard reports).

• KMS options: 1) Preferred: customer-managed KMS in your Azure/AWS account; 2) Fallback: envelope keys provided by you with Redwood HSM for node-level wrapping. Details in Appendix B.

• Backups & deletion: Redwood will provide signed deletion manifests and audit logs for primary stores. For cloud-managed immutable snapshots we will provide the deletion schedule and evidence of object-level deletions where supported by the provider.

• SCCs & STOMs: Attached addendum includes a STOM annex and a subprocessors table; we propose a 30-day notice for subprocessor changes and a constrained right-to-audit.

Next steps: please confirm if the attached addendum is acceptable to Counsel. If yes, we can route the doc for DocuSign. If you want a short technical walkthrough, I can book 30 minutes with Jordan and Ben this week — prefer Tue/Wed mornings (CEST).

If any of the summaries above require stronger binding language (e.g., explicit KMS custody guarantees or different deletion proof), flag the exact clause and we will escalate to Product & Legal for refinement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
